name: NJM2068 / JRC2068 (low-noise bipolar dual, New JRC → Nisshinbo)
tagline: A cheap, quiet JRC bipolar dual. NwAvGuy used it for the O2's gain stage, and it is common in E-MU audio interfaces and in Japanese CD and AV gear.
technology: Bipolar dual op-amp with the standard 4558 dual pinout. NJR's own SPICE macro-model uses a PNP input pair. Internally compensated. The features list calls 27 MHz the 'unity gain bandwidth', but the table gives GB 27 MHz at 10 kHz and a unity-gain frequency of only 5.5 MHz. The noise-selected D-rank grades (DD/MD/LD) have a guaranteed maximum equivalent input noise.
manufacturers: New Japan Radio Co., Ltd. (NJR; 'JRC' logo/brand)

reputation.summary: NwAvGuy measured the NJM2068 for the Objective2 (O2) and chose it for the gain stage. By his account it was quieter than the NE5532, LM4562 and OPA2134 at lower supply current, and it cost well under a dollar. That made it a favourite with the measurement-minded DIY community. The DIY SmartStand amp also copies the O2's NJM2068 gain stage with an NJM4556A output. In China, Soomal reviews found it in E-MU interfaces (0202/0204/0404/1212m), the Musiland X-Sword II and ooAoo sound cards, and many mid-range CD players. Soomal describes it as very low noise and high resolution, with a neutral, plain sound. Japanese op-amp swappers treat it as the classic quiet JRC dual, calling it relaxed with ample bass. Pro and MI gear uses it too: the Roland VG-99 input stage and GK-3 pickup (per h-milz), Yamaha and Pioneer AV and car units, and cheap MM phono preamps such as FX-Audio. The sound descriptors are community impressions, not measurements.
sonic_descriptors: very low noise (噪声很小; Soomal)
typical_uses: Chinese PC sound cards (Musiland X-Sword II, ooAoo SQ710 II/SQ717a)
mid-range Japanese CD players and AV receivers (e.g. Yamaha YSP-600 uses NJM2068MD-TE2)
guitar-synth/pro-audio input stages (Roland VG-99, GK-3 per h-milz)
active monitor speakers (ICON PX-T6A per Soomal)
caveats: Vendor notice: capacitive loads can cause oscillation. Add about 50 Ohm in series with the output (Ver.2011-03-18 p.2).
Minimum supply is +/-4 V (8 V total), so it is unsuitable for 5 V single-supply or USB-powered designs.
The '27 MHz' headline figure is GB at 10 kHz. The unity-gain frequency is only 5.5 MHz, so it is not comparable with other vendors' GBW numbers.
No noise-current or nV/rtHz spec, and input bias current is relatively high (150 nA typ, 1 uA max). Keep source and feedback impedances low.
Output current is not specified, and specs are given for loads of 2 kOhm and above. It is not a headphone driver: the O2 pairs it with NJM4556A outputs.

jh4vaj's pop-noise comparison found the standard NJM2068D had less turn-on pop than the noise-selected NJM2068DD. Both were among the low-pop group; NJM4558DD had the least. This is a single blog measurement.
A note.com blog (gokurakugadget) reports NJM2068D oscillating abnormally in an audio preamp. It is a single user report; see the vendor capacitive-load notice.

revision_history.changes: Oldest version found (Octopart copy filed under NJM2068M). No change log is printed. Differences from Ver.2011-03-18 are not established.

No change log is printed; NJR datasheets carry only a Ver. date footer. Both the English and the Japanese (Akizuki) editions carry this Ver. Content: supply +/-4 to +/-18 V (abs max +/-18 V); VNI 0.44 typ / 0.56 max uV (FLAT+JIS-A, Rs=300 Ohm); D-rank max 1.4 uV (RIAA, Rs=2.2 kOhm), DIP/DMP/SIP only; GB 27 MHz at 10 kHz and 19 MHz at 100 kHz; fT 5.5 MHz; SR 6 V/us; Ib max 1000 nA; Icc 5/8 mA; packages DIP8, DMP8, SIP8, SSOP8; notice to add about 50 Ohm in series for capacitive loads. It still circulates under the Nisshinbo listing on Octopart.
The 6-page edition on alldatasheet (ids 512047-512052) names NJM2068E, a part not in the 5-page Ver.2011-03-18. That suggests a package was added (EMP8/SOP8?). Ver. and date not seen.

This is the oldest Japanese-edition Ver. found (Marutsu copy njm2068d.pdf; title '2回路入り低雑音オペアンプ'). It is dated 3 days before the English Ver.2003-03-17, so the J and E editions of the 2003 issue were released together. No change log is printed, and differences from the Japanese Ver.2011-03-18 (Akizuki copy) are not established.

More copies were confirmed by result titles: the Mouser URL njr_njm2068_e-551643.pdf (already listed, revision previously 'unknown') holds Ver.2011-03-18, as do Mouser NJM2068_E-1917171.pdf and Octopart NJM2068V-TE1 (13544402). No change log is printed. The search summary repeats the content: 0.56 uV typ noise, 6 V/us, 27 MHz, packages DIP8/DMP8/SIP8/SSOP8, operating voltage +/-4 to +/-18 V.

counterfeit_notes: No NJM2068-specific counterfeit or remarking reports were found in a limited web search. Generic Amazon and eBay listings sell 'NJM2068M SOP8 JRC2068' in lots of 5-10 from unnamed sellers. As with other popular 'JRC' audio duals, such marketplace parts carry a general risk of being remarked. Buy from authorized distributors (Mouser, DigiKey, Akizuki). A 'DD'/'MD' marking only means noise-selected, not a different die, so a big price premium for 'DD' from unknown sellers deserves suspicion. Check the logo style, lot codes and package: genuine DMP8 has a 5.3 mm-wide body, not a 3.9 mm JEDEC SOIC, even though listings call it 'SOP8'.
alternatives: NJM4580 (Nisshinbo): similar noise floor and slightly better THD per h-milz; drop-in dual
NJM2114 (Nisshinbo): JRC's faster, 'higher-performance 2068' per the JP community
NJM5532 / NE5532: classic low-noise bipolar dual (check vendor die revisions)
LM4562 / LME49720 (TI): lower distortion, higher drive
NJM8068 (Nisshinbo): newer low-noise dual in SOP8 (e.g. NJM8068G-TE2); not compared here
open_questions: Which Ver. is the current Nisshinbo NJM2068_E.pdf, and does it change any limits? The claimed Ib 500 nA / Icc 7 mA is unsupported; every web copy found shows 1000 nA / 8 mA.
What changed between Ver.2003-03-17 and Ver.2011-03-18? Are there versions before 2003 (JRC data-book era)? The introduction year is not established.
The 6-page edition naming NJM2068E (alldatasheet 512051): what is its Ver./date, what is the NJM2068E package, and is it orderable?
Lifecycle of NJM2068D/DD/M/MD/V/LD. Only NJM2068L is confirmed EOL (Mouser). Is NJM2068 on Nisshinbo's NRND/discontinued lists?
A web summary quotes the features line as '0.56 uV typ', while the table read earlier gives 0.44 typ / 0.56 max. Confirm the features-line wording.

No PCN or die/fab change for NJM2068 was found. The JRC to NJR to Nisshinbo rebrand appears to be branding only (Nisshinbo listings still carry Ver.2011-03-18), but this is unconfirmed. Old-lot vs new-lot sound claims remain anecdotal.
The NwAvGuy measurements, the Headphonesty article and the bluegourd eid=388 post were not re-verified by web search this session.
